answer: The juniper multiplier is published, charged in sonnet, and ivory lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 503 identities would post 1112 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
